lines.note: Completes f201's example: the head of the thief is held firmly. This actual opening confirms the preceding bottom-right a ca- as a catchword.
Hittsutsumi, hittsutsumu, hittsutsunda is wrapping rapidly. The Portuguese preſ continues into ſa below; do not insert a division mark merely because the word continues.

runs.text: ſa. ¶ Item, Cercar com gente fortale-

lines.note: After completing pressa, the entry adds surrounding a fortress with men. This extends the enclosing sense of tsutsumu to a military operation.
Za completes fortaleza; the short fragment is running text ending the siege gloss, not independent furniture.

runs.text: Hũs ferros compridos do freo em que ſe

lines.note: Hitte names the long iron pieces of a horse's bit. The definition continues with their attachment function.
The horse's reins are tied to those pieces. This completes the hardware description rather than defining reins themselves.

runs.text: Certo eſpaço, ou lugar na porta de papel

lines.note: A second hitte is the gripping place on a paper door. The distinct headword repetition is intentional, with a different object and use.

runs.text: por onde aferrão pera abrir, ou fechar.

lines.note: The place is grasped to open or close the door. The scan joins aferrão; OCR's a ferrão incorrectly separates the verb, although the meaning remains recoverable.
Hittoo is paraphrased fude kashira, the brush or pen tip. The example begins with the repeated headword divided after Fit.
Hittoo ni tsukushigatashi means difficult to exhaust in writing. The Portuguese explains inability to finish writing it, rather than physical damage to a pen.
De escrever completes the writing expression. S. labels written usage; its italic appearance is retained in the apparatus.
Hittoki, hittoku, hittoita means untying. Carague- starts the binding-rope object in the example on the following row.
Karagenawa wo kurukuru to hittoita describes briskly undoing a binding rope. Tog. is a citation label, not a Japanese word belonging to the example.

runs.text: ſatou com preßa, & viueza a corda de a-

lines.note: The Portuguese explicitly translates the speed and vigour of untying the rope. A- continues into amarrar below.
Marrar completes amarrar, specifying the rope's use for binding. Its brevity does not make it disposable layout material.
Hittori here means withdrawing camp or returning from warfare. The alternative sense on the following rows must not be conflated with this military one.
Jin wo hittoru repeats the withdrawal-of-camp sense. Initial Gi represents the voiced Japanese syllable in jin, not hard gi.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Arrebatar, ou tomar por força da

lines.note: The entry adds snatching or forcibly taking something from a hand. This is a separate application of the same pulling-away verb.
Mão completes the source from which something is snatched. Retain its printed tilde carrier rather than mechanically matching other maõ spellings.

runs.text: Caſca de hũa aruore como acipreste.

lines.note: Hiwada is bark of a tree compared with cypress. The next roofing entry makes its construction use clear; the comparison is not a precise modern taxonomic identification.

runs.text: Otelhar com eſta caſca, ou cor-

lines.note: Hiwadabuki is roofing with this bark or cork. Portuguese O telhar is written Otelhar here; the initial O is not part of the Japanese headword.
Hiwadabuki no ie supplies the concrete example of a bark-roofed house. Telha continues into telhada on the next physical line without an imposed hyphen.

runs.text: da destas caſcas, ou cortiça de Finoqi.

lines.note: The roof is made from these barks, specifically hinoki bark. Finoqi is embedded Japanese, visibly italic here rather than automatically romanized.

runs.text: Cor que tira para preto ſobre ver-

lines.note: Hiwadairo, bark colour, is described as blackish over red. The scan's r and the colour compound iro both support correcting OCR's Fiuadaito.
Melho completes vermelho, red, in the preceding colour definition. This is not a separate colour term or entry.
Hiware, hiwaruru, hiwareta describes cracking or opening under sun exposure. The Japanese stem and the Portuguese fender are mutually consistent.
The sun is the cause of the cracking. The split cou/ſa belongs to one Portuguese noun and is retained at the physical break.
Hiwazzuna describes something weak and delicate. The gloss fits the hiwazu adjective family; preserve the printed double z rather than substitute a modern spelling.
Hiuba is glossed great-grandmother. The visibly accented final Portuguese vowel is retained; the Japanese spelling is not silently expanded to modern hiibaba.
Hiuchi denotes a fire-striking steel, not a modern firearm despite Portuguese fuzil. Fiuchide begins hiuchi de hi wo utsu; the scan supports ch rather than OCR's eh.
Hi wo utsu completes striking fire with the steel. The Portuguese repeats that instrumental action exactly.

runs.text: Bolſa da feição deſte fuzil q̃

lines.note: Hiuchibukuro is a pouch shaped like this fire-striking implement. The relative q̃ introduces how it is carried on the next row.
The pouch hangs from the belt. Dependurada is retained as printed rather than replaced by a modern preferred spelling.
Hiuchikado comprises steel and flint. X. is the regional label and is upright; it is not part of the headword or Portuguese object name.
Hiuchi no ishi is flint. The scan supports Fiuchino and ſe diz, correcting Fiachino and fe; the sentence introduces the Ximo regional equivalent below.
Kado is that regional word for flint. Although alone on a short row, it continues the preceding definition and is not page furniture.

Taka no hiugazu concerns a hawk from Hyuga. Falcão has a visible c missing from OCR. The Japanese u accent is damaged or one-sided; the provisional grave-shaped transcription is retained pending a clearer visual distinction.

runs.text: ſe criou, ou veo do reino de

lines.note: The bird was bred in or came from Hyuga province. Fiũga is entirely upright in the scan; the nasal-looking accent is retained without imposing the expected pronunciation.

runs.text: Pintura à maneira de abano, ou a-

lines.note: Hiwoogi is a fan-shaped painting or a painted fan. The marked o is visibly open-topped; do not replace it with a circumflex on lexical expectation alone.
Bano completes abano pintado, the painted-fan alternative. The short continuation is complete within its crop.
Hiuna is cross-referenced to hiyu and glossed bredos, edible amaranth greens. Fiyu is a Japanese cross-reference, not part of the Portuguese prose.
Hisha is explained literally as tobu kuruma, a flying vehicle. The dictionary first describes a vehicle moving through the air, before adding other senses.

runs.text: pellos ares, de que ſe falla nos liuros. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Such airborne vehicles are said to occur in books. This qualification matters: the gloss reports literary usage rather than asserting an ordinary contemporary vehicle.

runs.text: Carro ligeiro. ¶ Item, Caualo peça do ẽ-

lines.note: Further senses are a swift vehicle and a Japanese chess piece. Preserve the printed cavalo comparison even though hisha normally names the rook, not the modern chess knight.
Xadrez de Iapão completes the reference to Japanese chess or shogi. Do not silently correct the preceding European piece analogy.

runs.text: Hũa maneira de coco com ſeu cabo pe

lines.note: Hishaku is a handled dipper described by comparison with a coconut-shell vessel. The terminal pe continues pera below without a newly supplied hyphen.
Ra tirar agoa completes the purpose, drawing water. This short final line closes the dipper entry and remains body text.

runs.text: Vaſo onde poem o coco metendo o

lines.note: Hishakutate is the vessel holding a dipper with its handle inserted. The damaged terminal article reads o, not OCR's d; the right rule is visible and the crop does not conceal an ascender.
Cabo dentro completes the instruction to put the handle inside. This defines the stand by its use rather than a different kind of dipper.
Hisen is paraphrased iyashii koto, baseness. The i, is the explanatory abbreviation, not a Japanese vowel to be read with the next phrase.
The Portuguese adds low and contemptible, then introduces hisen na mono. The example divides mono across rows.
No completes mono, a low or vile person in this example. Peßoa retains the ligature convention and is not rewritten as modern pessoa.
A different hisen is tobu izzumi, a leaping stream or waterfall. The definition begins a rush of water; it is unrelated to the preceding social evaluation.

runs.text: agoa que cae de algum rochedo ou lugar alto.

lines.note: Water falls from a rock or high place. The visible shapes support rochedo even where ink is weak; this completes the waterfall description.
Hiset, glossed zooset, denotes false or uncertain reports. The final t is a historical coda, not an accidentally truncated modern setsu spelling.
The entry adds errors and false doctrine. The scan shows the ct group in doctrina, not OCR's st; the conventional term and visible type agree.
A distinct hiset is iyashuu tsutanai, low and poor. The adverbial long u and the Portuguese low/unclean gloss distinguish it from false reports.
Munda completes immunda. Although it resembles an independent word when isolated, the preceding im supplies the negative adjective's beginning.
Hishi denotes caltrops or spiked obstacles. Hishi wo ma- begins the example scattering them, not the aquatic plant sense below.

runs.text: Por abrolhos, ou meter estrepes pera

lines.note: Ku completes maku. The Portuguese describes placing caltrops to obstruct passage, maintaining the military sense.

runs.text: impedir algum caminho. No Ximo ſe diz

lines.note: The purpose is obstructing a road; a regional Ximo formulation follows. Ximo occurs within Portuguese explanatory prose.
Hishi wo uyuru or tatsuru are the regional alternatives, literally planting or setting up caltrops. They are Japanese examples, not Portuguese loans.
Idem explicitly equates those regional expressions with the preceding action. It is a complete short body continuation.

runs.text: Certa fruita de erua que ſe dà nas ala-

lines.note: This hishi is the fruit of an aquatic plant, consistent with water caltrop. The Portuguese locates its growth in ponds or lakes rather than describing the military implement.
Goas completes alagoas. Keep the older expanded form rather than normalize it to lagoas.
Hishi, hisuru, hishita means concealing. This Sino-Japanese verb is distinguished by the gloss from the identically inflected comparison verb immediately below.
Hishi here means comparing. Ware iki- begins the example about the speaker's power; Vt is an italic introduction, not part of the Japanese sentence.
Ikioi nangira ni hishoozuru mono de nai says the speaker's power cannot compare with the addressee's. Historical nangira and the contracted future/volitional-looking form should not be modernized.

runs.text: nha força, & poder não he pera ſe comparar

lines.note: Minha força e poder gives the Portuguese counterpart of ikioi. The negative comparison continues into com vosco on the next row.
Com voſco supplies the addressee. The visible separation is retained rather than modernized to convosco.
Hishiko is a kind of fish brine or salted-fish preparation. The gloss names a preparation, not necessarily the fish in the following entry.
A second hishiko is a particular fish. The short definition does not justify adding a modern species identification to the transcription.
Hishikui is a bird compared with a wild duck. The familiar goose name is compatible, but the source's comparison remains unchanged.
Hishihishito is an adverb of speed, force, or closeness. Adu. and the explanatory prose are italic; the scope broadens across the following examples.
Rijamente and apertadamente add forcefully and tightly. The repeated Japanese adverb is divided after Fixi- in the example.
Hishihishito utaruru means being beaten severely. The passive Japanese verb and Portuguese ser espancado agree.
Zashiki ni hishihishito nami iru describes sitting closely in rows. Both Japanese syntax and the visible a support correcting OCR's Zxxiqini to Zaxiqini.

runs.text: todos no Zaxiqui aßentados por ordem, &a-

lines.note: Everyone is seated in order and tightly in the zashiki. Zaxiqui is embedded Japanese in the Portuguese gloss and visibly italic here.
Pertados completes apertados, crowded closely together. The continuation belongs to the seating example, not a new entry.
Hishige, hishiguru, hishigeta is becoming crushed or broken. The reflexive Portuguese distinguishes it from the transitive hishigu entry below.
Çarſe completes esmiuçar-se, crumbling or breaking into small pieces. The initial cedilla belongs to the continued word.
Hishigi, hishigu, hishiida means breaking or crushing. The printed ijda records the historical contracted past; do not replace it with a modern textbook form.
After crushing with blows, fue wo hishigu introduces a special flute-playing use. Its sense must be read from the following explanation, not forced into literal destruction of a flute.

runs.text: car leuemente afrauta nos autos, feſtas de tan-

lines.note: The flute is played lightly in performances and music-and-dance festivities. Autos is supported by the visible u and this context, correcting OCR's antos.

runs.text: ger, & bailar, como quando começão a tãger,

lines.note: The light playing occurs as performers begin to play or dance. Começão and tãger retain their historical spelling and abbreviation.
Ou acabão adds the ending of the performance as another occasion. It completes the special musical usage of hishigu.
Hishimeki names bustle, commotion, or noise. The Portuguese rebuliço and estrondo support that nominal sense.
Hishimeki, hishimeku, hishimeita is the corresponding verb. The historical -eita past is retained rather than normalized to a modern form.
Buliço completes rebuliço. This short continuation closes the verbal definition.
Hishimekiai, hishimekioo, hishimekioota expresses commotion among several people. Both o accents are visibly caron-shaped in the scan.
Traquinada entre algũs completes the reciprocal or collective disturbance. The nasal abbreviation is retained as printed.
Hishito means wholly or deliberately. Its damaged initial capital does not undermine the clear following letters and matching example.
Efficazmente adds effectively; the scan supports c rather than OCR's r. Hishito utsu then illustrates striking firmly.
The gloss is striking hard or driving a nail. Rijamente, not OCR's riſamente, is supported by the descending j and the action described.
Bottom-right anticipation of the next page's opening. Retained with its stable ID as catchword furniture rather than counted twice in the running definition.
